answer: Coordination Ridge Pricing. Each agent action carries a fee equal to the current coordination load on its interaction neighborhood, measured as the ridge of recent pairwise contacts, so fees rise steeply where many identities cluster. To register, an attacker must pay the prevailing ridge price for every identity, and any timber of synthetic cross-links raises the load it pays on, compounding cost per added node. Honest sparse agents sit on a low dune of contact density and pay little. Attacker cost scales with cluster width, not headcount.
